title: AP CSP — Lesson 18 Homework: Traversing Lists
notice: All questions are original. Q1–Q6 are AP-style practice, not official AP questions. Q7–Q12 and all marks are teacher-designed. Q5 earns one mark only for both correct choices and no others. Q5: select exactly TWO. FOR EACH visits each element value in order. Keep the source list unchanged; append matches to a new list. Code braces go on separate lines.

questions.explanation: B uses 1-based index 2. A is first; C confuses index and value; D is the length.

questions.prompt: FOR EACH item IN [10, 30, 20] assigns which values to item in order?
questions.explanation: C follows element order. A and B use indices. D sorts without an instruction.

questions.prompt: Where should total ← 0 be placed to sum an entire list?

options.label: C
options.text: At the end of every visit

questions.explanation: D initializes once. A and C repeatedly discard progress. B initializes too late.

questions.prompt: How many loop-body executions occur for FOR EACH item IN [6, 6, 6]?
questions.explanation: A counts three elements. B deduplicates without permission. C confuses values with count. D ignores the elements.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements match this lesson’s filter design? Select exactly TWO answers.

options.label: A
options.text: Remove nonmatches from the source during traversal.

options.label: C
options.text: Append each matching occurrence to that result.

options.label: D
options.text: Sort the source automatically before filtering.

questions.explanation: B and C build a stable separate result. A changes the traversed source and violates the design. D adds an unrequested sort; filtering preserves source order here.

questions.prompt: total starts at 0, then each value in [] is added to it. What is the final total?

options.label: A
options.text: An invalid index is always accessed

questions.explanation: D remains initialized 0 because there are no visits. A assumes indexed access not present. B invents an increment. C refers to a nonexistent element.

questions.prompt: Start total=0. Add each value in [5, 10, 5] during FOR EACH. Give (a) total after visit 1, (b) after visit 2, (c) after visit 3, and (d) the number of visits.
Start selected=[]. For each value in [12, 30, 30, 45], append it when value ≥ 30. Give selected after each of the four visits.
Write code that sets total to 0, visits each minutes value in sessions, adds it to total, and displays the final total after traversal. Assume sessions is a numeric list.

rubric.criterion: Initializes total to 0 before the loop.
Uses FOR EACH to visit sessions values.
Adds current minutes to the running total inside the loop.

questions.prompt: Write code that creates selected=[] and appends each value from sessions that is at least goal. Preserve sessions and its order. sessions is numeric and goal is a number.

rubric.criterion: Appends each matching current value to selected inside the condition, preserving order.

questions.prompt: A filter keeps values ≥ 30. Give the resulting list for (a) [29], (b) [30], (c) [31], and (d) [].

For each value in [4, 7, 2], a program first sets total=0 and then adds the value to total. (a) Give its final total. (b) State the fix. (c) Give the corrected total. (d) Explain why changing the source during a separate filtering traversal is avoided here.
questions.answer: (a) 2. (b) Initialize total once before traversal. (c) 13. (d) Keeping the source unchanged prevents shifts from altering which elements are visited and preserves data for checking.
questions.explanation: (a) 2. (b) Initialize total once before traversal. (c) 13. (d) Keeping the source unchanged prevents shifts from altering which elements are visited and preserves data for checking.

rubric.criterion: Explains stable visits or preserving the original data as a concrete reason.
